lede: The biggest decision point this week comes Monday and Tuesday, when Norwood's Planning and Zoning Commission takes up Phase I of a full Land Use Code rewrite — the kind of thing that quietly sets the rules for development and density for years to come — while Telluride's Town Council holds public hearings on converting two affordable ownership units at 215 East Colorado Avenue into employee dwelling units and removing their price caps. The school board also votes Tuesday on resolutions backing Proposition NN and Amendment 87, and the County commissioners continue a public hearing on adopting new International Building Codes on Wednesday.

notable.stake: Norwood votes to adopt Land Use Code amendments shaping local development rules.
Board votes on state ballot measure resolutions and second-reading policy changes.
Resolution would convert two affordable ownership units, removing maximum sale price.
Public hearings on deed-restriction conversion that removes price caps on two units.
Commission considers new leak check fee and rules on six leak forgiveness requests.
Continued public hearing on new building codes that will govern future construction countywide.
